test_title: PYST 54: SSC CPO - General Knowledge and General Awareness (Held on 04 Oct, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: gk
question: Choose the INCORRECT statement out of the following.

options.text: Most parts of the country receive rainfall from June to September.
The annual precipitation in Meghalaya is over 400 cm.
Some parts like the Tamil Nadu’s coast gets a large portion of its rains during October and November.
There is increase in rainfall generally from east to west in the Northern Plains.

solution:
The correct answer is** **__**Option 4**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

 
• The monsoon season in India typically occurs from **June to September**.

 
 
• It is a **critical period** for the country as it brings the much-needed **rainfall** that replenishes water sources,including rivers, lakes, and groundwater. 
 
• Agriculture heavily relies on monsoon rains for **crop cultivation**, making it a lifeline for farmers.
 
• Hence** Statement 1 is Correct.**
 
 
 
• ** Meghalaya, **known for its heavy rainfall, receives an annual precipitation of over 400 cm.(**about 160 inches)**
 
 
• **Cherrapunji (** located in Meghalaya**)** held the record for the **highest annual rainfall** for many years.
 
• Hence **Statement 2 is correct.**
 
 
 
• The **northeast monsoon**, also known as the **retreating monsoon**, affects Tamil Nadu’s coastal regions.
 
 
• It occurs during the **post-monsoon period**, primarily from **October to December**.
 
• Cities like **Chennai**, **Puducherry**, and **Cuddalore** experienced heavy showers during this period.
 
• The rain is crucial for **agriculture**, groundwater recharge, and overall water availability.
 
• Hence **Statement 3 is also Correct.**
 
 
 
• In the **Northern Plains**, which include states like **Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar**, the rainfall pattern is East to West.
 
 
• ​Rainfall decreases as we move from east to west.
 
• Hence the **statement 4 is incorrect.**
